items.excerpt: University at Buffalo researchers paired Raman spectroscopy with a neural network to identify four organelles inside living cells at about 90% accuracy, with no fluorescent dyes. The dye-free 'Ramanomics' route removes a long-standing obstacle to watching cells without perturbing them.

Emory and Georgia Tech researchers built CapuchinAI, a field system combining facial recognition with touchscreen cognitive tasks for wild capuchin monkeys. It identified individual monkeys with 97% accuracy in Costa Rica, moving primate cognition testing out of the lab.

Nearly one in five people aged 12-21 now turn to AI chatbots for mental health guidance, a 60% jump in a single year, according to Harvard researchers. Most of those youths told no adult they were doing it.

Two physicists, one of them a Nobel laureate, cracked a decade-old puzzle about jamming transitions with help from Claude. The account is a concrete look at how an AI model slots into a working theory-physics collaboration rather than replacing it.

OpenAI's claimed AI-generated math advances are drawing accusations of research misconduct, with mathematicians saying prior work went uncited. The dispute is becoming a test case for how AI-produced results get credited in science.

After eight years, 200 million predictions and a Nobel Prize, Google DeepMind has dissolved its dedicated AlphaFold team. The lab argues the problem is largely solved and outside researchers are already carrying the work forward.

A cognitive-science-inspired AI framework organizes information into 'cognitive maps', solving planning problems more adaptively while using far less energy. The design is aimed at neuromorphic hardware rather than ever-larger transformer stacks.

KAIST built a programmable dynamic memtransistor that retunes its own response speed to match time-series data arriving at different rates. Prediction errors dropped up to 40-fold against fixed-response devices.

Georgia Tech will lead an $18.1M NSF-funded National Cloud Laboratory that gives researchers nationwide remote access to its Advanced Manufacturing Pilot Facility. The plan pairs AI with autonomous experimentation across more than 100 pieces of equipment.

Schrödinger CEO Ramy Farid explains what changed his mind about AI's role alongside physics-based drug design. It is a rare account of a computational-chemistry veteran revising his model of where learned models beat first-principles simulation.
